exhibits.title: Spot Price
exhibits.statement: Bitcoin (BTC) traded at $65,596.00 as of 2026-11-15 09:25:54 UTC, +1.24% over one hour and -2.16% over twenty-four hours.

exhibits.title: 24-Hour Trading Range
exhibits.statement: Over twenty-four hours the price ranged from $62,081.00 to $67,368.00; spot sits at 67% of that range.

exhibits.title: Seven-Day Trend
exhibits.statement: Price is -14.65% over seven days. The 24-hour average ($65,228.95) is below the 72-hour average ($68,186.42). Spot is 13.67% below the seven-day high of $75,986.18 and 5.66% above the seven-day low of $62,081.00.

exhibits.title: Volatility & Momentum
exhibits.statement: Realized volatility computed from hourly closes is 3.07% per day. The 14-hour relative strength index reads 50.4, conventionally neutral.

exhibits.title: Liquidity
exhibits.statement: Twenty-four-hour trading volume was $55.58 billion, equal to 4.21% of the $1.32 trillion market capitalization.

exhibits.title: Market Sentiment
exhibits.statement: The Crypto Fear & Greed Index reads 10 ("Extreme Fear"), versus 28 7 days earlier.

exhibits.title: Chainlink Price Feed
exhibits.statement: The Chainlink BTC/USD Data Feed on Ethereum mainnet last reported $65,659.40, 22 minutes before the spot quote and +0.10% against the spot price in Exhibit A. Practice positions are entered and settled at this mark.

arguments.text:
May it please the Court.  

1. The spot price is firmly anchored at $65,596, up 1.24% in the last hour and sitting at 67% of the 24‑hour range, indicating a short‑term bullish bias within a bounded market [Ex. A, B].  

2. Despite a seven‑day decline, realized volatility remains modest at 3.07% per day and the RSI of 50.4 signals neutral momentum, allowing a controlled long position to capture upside without excessive risk [Ex. D, C].  

3. Market sentiment is at an extreme fear level of 10, historically preceding rebounds, while the Chainlink feed confirms a slightly higher price of $65,659, providing a reliable entry point for the practice trade [Ex. F, G].  

The Bull rests.

May it please the Court.  

1. The market is in a pronounced downtrend, with price down 14.65% over seven days and the 24‑hour average $65,229 still below the 72‑hour average $68,186, indicating weakening support and a bias toward further decline [Ex. C].  

2. Liquidity remains robust at $55.58 billion (4.21% of market cap), ensuring ample depth for a short trade without slippage, while realized volatility of 3.07% per day provides sufficient price movement to capture profit [Ex. D, E].  

3. Fear dominates sentiment, as the Fear & Greed Index plunged to 10 (“Extreme Fear”) from 28 a week earlier, historically preceding continued price drops, and the Chainlink feed corroborates the spot price at $65,659, confirming a reliable entry level for a short position [Ex. F, G].  

The Bear rests.

Your Honor, the Bear’s downtrend claim ignores that the price is currently positioned 67 % up the 24‑hour range, indicating buying pressure near the upper bound rather than a collapse [Ex. B]; a range‑bound market often rebounds. Moreover, the volatility cited is modest—3.07 % per day—far below the thresholds that generate meaningful short‑term profit, especially when the RSI is neutral at 50.4, showing no oversold condition to fuel a decline [Ex. D]. Hence the Bear lacks a compelling edge for a short. Nothing further.

Your Honor, the Bull leans on a fleeting one‑hour gain and a “neutral” RSI, yet Exhibit C shows a 14.65% seven‑day plunge and a 24‑hour average $65,229 still below the 72‑hour average $68,186, evidencing sustained bearish pressure; short‑term spikes cannot override that trend. Moreover, Exhibit D’s volatility of 3.07% per day is not “modest” in crypto terms and, coupled with the RSI of 50.4—exactly the midpoint—offers no bullish momentum, only indecision, undermining the claim of a “controlled long” advantage. Consequently, the data do not support opening a practice long position. Nothing further.

ruling.holding: The Court finds the evidence supports a short practice position.

findings.finding: Bitcoin has fallen 14.65% over seven days and the 24‑hour average remains below the 72‑hour average, indicating a downtrend.
Fear & Greed Index at 10 (Extreme Fear) shows market pessimism, historically linked to further declines.
Realized volatility of 3.07% per day provides sufficient price movement for a short trade, while RSI 50.4 is neutral, offering no bullish momentum.
Spot sits at 67% of the 24‑hour range, but this is still below the seven‑day high, indicating limited upward pressure.

ruling.opinion: The seven‑day price decline and lower short‑term average (Ex. C) establish a bearish trend that outweighs the modest bullish signal of a 67% range position (Ex. B). Extreme fear (Ex. F) typically precedes further drops, and volatility of 3.07% per day (Ex. D) supplies the movement needed for a short. Neutral RSI offers no confirmation of upside, so the balance favors a short position.
ruling.dissent: Bull counsel stresses the 67% range position and neutral RSI as signs of a rebound, but these are outweighed by the sustained seven‑day downtrend and extreme fear indicating continued downside.
